findings.summary: The stable percent-decoding policy is duplicated across author-document and SLA article sanitizers.
findings.consequence: A future fix to encoded traversal or malformed percent handling can land in one raw-HTML sanitizer but not the other, leaving author document links and SLA article links with different safety behavior despite protecting the same managed-content URL boundary.
findings.evidence: The owned `fullyDecode` function at line 207 implements the same 16-pass `decodeURIComponent` loop and fail-closed behavior as `server/utils/sla-article.ts` lines 186-198. `server/utils/sla-article.ts` already imports several author-document utilities, including URL-adjacent validation helpers, so the duplicate decoder is not enforcing a separate policy.
findings.recommendation: Move the stable percent-decoder into a shared URL-safety helper, or export a narrowly named helper from `author-document.ts` and have `sla-article.ts` reuse it, preserving the current 16-pass fail-closed semantics and existing tests for deep encoded traversal.
